seoDescription: Learn to master promotions in Magento 2 by understanding the key differences between Catalog Price Rules and Cart Price Rules. This tutorial walks you through setting up discounts that apply as customers browse your catalog, such as a percentage off a specific category. You'll also learn how to create Cart Price Rules that activate during checkout, including how to configure specific coupon codes, manage usage limits, and auto-generate unique codes in bulk for marketing campaigns.

chapters.title: Catalog vs. Cart Price Rules
chapters.description: Introduces the two main promotion types in Magento 2 and explains their fundamental difference.

chapters.title: Creating a New Catalog Price Rule
chapters.description: Walks through setting up the general information for a new catalog price rule, including its name, status, scope, and schedule.

chapters.title: Configuring Catalog Rule Conditions, Actions & Priority
chapters.description: Details how to set conditions to target specific products, define the discount action, and manage rule priority and subsequent rule processing.

chapters.title: Applying the Rule & Advanced Conditions
chapters.description: Covers the essential step of applying the rule to make it live, verifying the result on the frontend, and exploring more complex conditions.

chapters.title: Creating a Cart Price Rule with a Specific Coupon
chapters.description: Begins creating a cart price rule, focusing on the setup for a specific, manually-entered coupon code and its usage limits.

chapters.title: Cart Rule Conditions and Troubleshooting
chapters.description: Explains the wide array of cart-specific conditions available and demonstrates that a rule requires an action to have any effect.

chapters.title: Setting Cart Rule Actions and Applying the Coupon
chapters.description: Configures the discount action for the cart rule, sets up labels for the promotion, and successfully applies the coupon code in the shopping cart.

chapters.title: How to Auto-Generate Bulk Coupon Codes
chapters.description: Shows how to use Magento's powerful feature to automatically generate a large number of unique coupon codes for a promotion.

chapters.title: Conclusion
chapters.description: Provides a final summary of the tutorial and offers further assistance.

summary:
## Magento 2 Promotion Types

Magento offers two primary types of promotions under `Marketing > Promotions`:

- **Catalog Price Rules**: These promotions are applied directly in the catalog. Customers see the discounted price while browsing category or product pages, before adding anything to the cart.
- **Cart Price Rules**: These promotions are applied in the shopping cart and checkout phases. They can be automatic or triggered by a coupon code.

## Catalog Price Rules

Use these for site-wide or category-wide sales visible during browsing.

- **Conditions**: Define when the rule applies. A common condition is targeting a specific **product category**. You can combine multiple conditions using `ALL` (AND logic) or `ANY` (OR logic).
- **Actions**: Define what the promotion does.
  - `Apply as percentage of original`: Applies a percentage discount (e.g., 10% off).
  - `Apply as fixed amount`: Applies a specific monetary discount (e.g., $12 off).
- **Priority**: A numeric value (lower is higher priority) that determines which rule applies first if multiple rules match the same product. Use the `Discard subsequent rules` setting to prevent other, lower-priority rules from being applied.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> After saving a Catalog Price Rule, you must click **Apply Rules**. The promotion will not be live until Magento's indexer (cron job) processes the changes, which may take a minute or more.

## Cart Price Rules

Use these for more complex promotions that apply during checkout, often involving coupons.

- **Coupons**: You can set a rule to require a coupon.
  - **No Coupon**: The rule applies automatically if conditions are met.
  - **Specific Coupon**: You define a single coupon code (e.g., `FIVE_OFF`).
  - **Use Auto Generation**: Allows for generating unique codes in bulk.
- **Usage Limits**: Control how many times a coupon can be used.
  - **Uses per Coupon**: Total uses for the entire coupon code.
  - **Uses per Customer**: Limits how many times one logged-in customer can use the coupon.
- **Conditions**: Offers a much wider range of conditions than catalog rules, including:
  - Cart subtotal (e.g., spend over $100)
  - Shipping information (e.g., country, postcode)
  - Payment method
  - Product attribute combinations
- **Actions**: Define the discount.
  - `Percent of product price discount`: Standard percentage off.
  - `Free Shipping`: Can be offered for specific shipping methods.

> [!NOTE]
> A Cart Price Rule will not work until you define an **Action**. Simply setting up a coupon code and conditions is not enough; you must specify what discount the customer receives.

## How to Auto-Generate Coupon Codes

For large-scale campaigns, you can create many unique codes at once.

1.  In your Cart Price Rule, set **Coupon** to `Specific Coupon` and check the **Use Auto Generation** box.
2.  Go to the **Manage Coupon Codes** tab.
3.  Specify the **Coupon Qty** (how many codes to make), **Code Length**, and **Code Format** (alphanumeric, etc.).
4.  Optionally add a **Code Prefix** or **Suffix** for tracking (e.g., `HOLIDAYS-`).
5.  Click **Generate**.

> [!TIP]
> Once generated, you can view the list of unique codes, see their usage stats, and **export the list as a CSV or XML file** to use in newsletters and other marketing efforts.

## Catalog vs. Cart Price Rules

Buddy, this is Ori from Astro web and I'm going to show you how to manage promotions in Magento 2. So Magento has two types of promotions: one is the catalog price rule and the other one is Shopping Cart price rule or cart price rules right here.

If you go to the marketing section and promotions, the difference between the two of them is catalog price rules will actually, based on your rules, will make promotions when a user is browsing the site, when they're browsing the catalog. Either they're on a category page or on the product page, if the rules apply they'll see whatever promotion applies.

The cart price rules do exactly what it says, which is the promotion would be applied in the cart, in the checkout phases. So those are kind of two different things. Now the cart price rules by default has a few more options that you can do, and there's a few differences. Okay, so let's start with the catalog price rules right now.

Now each of them have their own pricing, this is 50 dollars and 50 and 120, etc. So what I want to do is actually make a promotion, either a dollar amount off, maybe ten dollars off, or a percentage off, maybe 10 percent, 20 percent off the entire catalog. So the entire shoes category, everything that is inside this category will have a promotion. So let's start. Okay.

So catalog price rules, I'm going to click on 'Add New'. Excuse me, let's see what happened here. Let's go catalog price rules and click on 'Add New'. Okay, great.

So now we're going to name the actual promotion itself. So let's do right now, twenty percent... let's do ten percent off, okay, all shoes products. So right now, I can... this is my name, it's mandatory. The description is an internal description for me to understand better about the promotion, but this is plenty for me. Okay, the status is active or not, which websites does it apply to, and also which groups does it apply to. Does it apply to a specific group, maybe a VIP group or a wholesale group or for everybody? So if it's for everybody and we allow guest checkout, we want to select all of them.

Now we have to select the timeframe, so I'm just going to do, let's say for the entire month right now. And then the priority. So priority is used to prioritize if multiple promotions apply during the same rule. So sometimes you might have multiple promotions running at the same time and you may or may not wish to have a customer be able to use more than one at a time.
